title: Influence of environmental variation and trophic interactions on the diet and growth of larval English sole (Parophrys vetulus)
content:
Abstract
Environmental conditions can influence larval fish growth and survival both directly through impacts on feeding and metabolism and indirectly through changes in prey and predator abundances that can alter feeding patterns and mortality. We examined the diet and daily growth of larval English sole (Parophrys vetulus), an abundant pleuronectiform species in winter ichthyoplankton of the northern California Current. We combined depth discrete net sampling with in situ plankton imaging over four winters (2018, 2019, 2022, and 2023) and four latitudinally varying cross-shelf transects (44–47°N) to assess the role of direct and indirect processes on growth of larvae. English sole larvae were specialized consumers of appendicularians across all sampling years, locations, and developmental stages. Cross-shelf position was a major driver of (i) differences in consumed prey size in postflexion larvae and (ii) recent larval growth at two of four sampling transects. Fish at the most nearshore stations consumed larger prey and grew faster. A piecewise structural equation model indicated that the direct effects of temperature and cross-shelf position were the primary variables explaining mean recent larval growth, while trophic (prey availability, predator abundance) and other indirect influences were comparatively small. Combined, our results suggest that English sole are not strongly prey-limited as larvae, and that their propensity for high abundance nearshore may enhance their growth and recruitment to shallow juvenile nursery areas.
